STRUCTURE FIRE - FRESHWATER ROAD
~ 10:15 a.m; An SJRFD Acting Platoon Chief has confirmed to NFLD Bulletin that the fire originated in the kitchen area of the home before spreading smoke throughout the residence and into both neighbouring attached homes. At least five residents have been assessed for smoke inhalation, with four of them transported to hospital for further assessment. Freshwater Road remains closed at this time.
~ 9:50 a.m; The incident appears to be under control. Firefighters are conducting overhaul operations. The road remains closed. More info soon. 
~ 9:20 a.m; Emergency crews are on the scene of a structure fire at a residential property on Freshwater Road in downtown St. John’s.
Freshwater Road between Lemerchant Road and Cookstown Road is fully closed.

COLLISION - OLD PLACENTIA RD/RICHARD NOLAN DR
(Nov 27)
~ 9:55 p.m; An SJRFD Captain has confirmed at the scene that there were no serious injuries present. Both vehicles have sustained extensive damage. Traffic remains slowed. 
~ 9:40 p.m.: The St. John’s Regional Fire Department (SJRFD) is on scene of a two-vehicle collision at the intersection of Old Placentia Road and Richard Nolan Drive in Mount Pearl.
Traffic is slowed in the area. Motorists should avoid the area if possible and expect delays. More information will be posted as it becomes available.

COLLISION - TCH NEAR GOOBIES
(Nov 27th)
~ 9:00 p.m; Emergency crews are on the scene of a motor vehicle collision on the Trans Canada Highway in front of NLC Liquor Express & Goobies North Atlantic.
Please use caution in the area.

JUNIPER RIDGE STUDENTS GRADUATE FROM RNC D.A.R.E. PROGRAM
(Nov 27th)
Students at Juniper Ridge Intermediate celebrated their graduation from the D.A.R.E. (Drug Abuse Resistance Education) program today, delivered by the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC).
Town of Torbay Councillor Jenny Whitten attended the celebration and presented a donation on behalf of the Town in support of the program.
D.A.R.E. aims to empower young people to make safe, healthy and responsible decisions while building confidence and positive relationships.
The Town of Torbay thanked the RNC, teachers, school staff and everyone involved in making the program a success, while congratulating all graduating students.
Town of Torbay.

BOWRING PARK HOLIDAY LIGHTS CELEBRATION SET FOR SATURDAY
(Nov 27th)
The City of St. John’s is inviting residents to kick off the holiday season this Saturday with the annual Holiday Lights celebration at Bowring Park.
The event takes place November 28th from 5 to 6 p.m. at the Bowring Park Duck Pond. 
The celebration will feature live performances by Cassandra Ingram and the Rev Dave Trio, free hot chocolate provided by the St. John’s Lions Club, and the official lighting of the park.
The Community Food Sharing Association will also be onsite accepting non-perishable food items and monetary donations.
In the event of adverse weather, the celebration will move to Saturday, December 5.
The holiday lights will remain on display nightly until January 7, 2027.
For general event inquiries, residents can contact 311.

DRIVER ARRESTED AFTER SPEEDING 70 KM/H OVER LIMIT IN SCHOOL ZONE, FLEEING POLICE
(Nov 27th)
A 22-year-old man is facing multiple charges after allegedly driving at speeds of up to 120 km/h in a 50 km/h school zone in Mobile before failing to stop for police Thursday afternoon.
On November 26, around 2:45 p.m., a Ferryland RCMP officer conducting proactive patrols on the Southern Shore Highway (Route 10) observed a vehicle travelling at a high rate of speed near the local high school.
Radar confirmed the vehicle was travelling at speeds of up to 120 km/h in the posted 50 km/h zone.
The officer immediately initiated a traffic stop, but the driver failed to comply with police emergency equipment and continued travelling at a high rate of speed, passing other vehicles in an unsafe manner.
Police followed the vehicle to a property in Tors Cove, where 22-year-old Brady Rodgers was arrested for flight from police and dangerous operation of a motor vehicle.
Rodgers was transported to the RCMP detachment in Holyrood, where he was held in custody overnight ahead of an appearance in provincial court today (November 27).
In addition to the Criminal Code charges, Rodgers was issued a ticket for excessive speed. His driver’s licence was suspended, and the vehicle he was operating was seized and impounded by police.
The RCMP reminds motorists that officers proactively patrol roadways throughout Newfoundland and Labrador to identify impaired drivers, check seatbelt use and ensure vehicles and drivers are operating safely with the appropriate documentation.
Motorists are reminded to drive safely, drive sober and ensure their driver’s licence, registration and insurance are up to date.

DRIVER ARRESTED IN SPANIARD’S BAY AFTER FLEEING RNC NEAR ST. JOHN’S
(Nov 27th)
A 20-year-old man is facing charges of dangerous driving and flight from police after fleeing a traffic stop initiated by the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) on the Trans-Canada Highway Thursday evening.
Around 7 p.m. on November 26, RNC Traffic Services officers were conducting routine patrols on the Trans-Canada Highway in the area of Thomas Pond when they observed a vehicle travelling more than 80 km/h over the posted speed limit.
Officers attempted to conduct a traffic safety stop, however, the driver failed to stop and fled in a dangerous manner.
Police did not pursue the vehicle in the interest of public safety. The RCMP was notified after the vehicle was last seen travelling westbound on Peacekeepers Way.
The 20-year-old driver was later arrested by RCMP officers at a residence in Spaniard’s Bay without incident.
He was charged with flight from police and dangerous driving. His vehicle was seized, and his driver’s licence was suspended.
The man was released and is scheduled to appear in court at a later date.
The RNC continues to encourage the public to report dangerous or impaired driving directly to police by calling 911.

ATTEMPTING TO LOCATE RIGHTFUL OWNER OF ITEM FOUND
(Nov 27th)
A member of the public is trying to reunite the owner of an expensive item with their property after it fell out of the back of a pickup truck in St. John’s Friday afternoon.
The item was found around 2:15 p.m. on November 27 at the intersection of Topsail Road and Brookfield Road, near the Brookfield Fire Station.
The individual who recovered the item says they are not publicly identifying what it is to ensure it is returned to the rightful owner.
Anyone who believes they may have lost the item is asked to send us a private message with details so we can put them in contact with the individual who currently has it.

MAN WITH OUTSTANDING WARRANTS ARRESTED
(Nov 27th)
A 36-year-old man from Grand Falls-Windsor was arrested in Deer Lake Thursday evening after RCMP officers located him during proactive offender management checks.
Just before 8:30 p.m. on November 26, officers with the RCMP West District General Investigation Section (GIS) and the RCMP-RNC Joint Forces Operation West were conducting checks at a business on Pennell’s Lane to ensure compliance with court-imposed conditions.
During the checks, officers located Robert Bennett-Reid, who was wanted on three outstanding warrants.
Bennett-Reid was wanted in connection with one count each of assault, theft under $5,000 and resisting or obstructing a peace officer, along with five counts of failure to comply with a probation order.
He was held in police custody overnight and is scheduled to appear in court today, November 27.
The RCMP says officers across Newfoundland and Labrador routinely conduct offender management checks to ensure individuals are complying with court-imposed conditions.
These initiatives target individuals known to police and are intended to help reduce repeat crime and enhance public safety through continued monitoring and follow-up checks.

FIRE INCIDENT - MOUNT PEARL
(Nov 27th)
~ 1:15 p.m; An SJRFD Captain has confirmed at the scene that the building experienced a power outage. When power was restored, an electrical short circuit occurred. No fire or smoke was found inside the building. Firefighters and other first responders are now clearing the scene.
~ 12:45 p.m; Emergency crews have responded to, and are currently on the scene of a reported electrical fire at a group of commercial businesses on Merchant Drive in Mount Pearl.
The businesses are currently evacuated.
More info soon. ￼

RCMP INVESTIGATING SUSPICIOUS FIRE THAT DESTROYED VACANT HOME
(Nov 27th)
Bay St. George RCMP is investigating a suspicious fire that destroyed a vacant residential property in Stephenville Crossing overnight.
Shortly before 12:30 a.m. on November 27, officers with the Bay St. George RCMP detachment and members of the Stephenville Crossing Volunteer Fire Department responded to a reported fire at a vacant home on Water Street.
No one was inside the residence at the time. However, the building was destroyed by the fire before it was extinguished.
Police say a witness reported seeing an unknown male leaving the area on foot around the time the fire was discovered. The witness was unable to provide a detailed description of the individual.
Investigators are asking anyone with information about the fire, or anyone with surveillance camera or dashcam footage from the Water Street area between 12:00 a.m. and 1:00 a.m. on November 27, to contact Bay St. George RCMP at 709-643-2118.
Anyone wishing to provide information anonymously can contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

COLLISION - PRINCE PHILIP DRIVE
(Nov 27th)
~ 9:00 a.m; Emergency crews are on the scene of a three-vehicle rear-end collision on Prince Philip Drive heading eastbound nearing the intersection to Wicklow Street in St. John’s. There are no injuries to reported.
Traffic remains slowed and down to one lane of travel.

MAN CHARGED AFTER EXPLOSIVES CLAIM AT ST. JOHN’S AIRPORT
(Nov 27th)
On Thursday evening (Nov 26th), At approximately 6:40 p.m; Officers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) Operational Patrol Services responded to St. John’s International Airport located at 100 World Parkway in St. John’s. 
Upon arrival, officers learned that a 39-year-old male had told airport staff he had a bag of explosives.
The male was arrested and charged under the Aeronautics Act with Interfering with the Operations of an Air Navigation Facility.
He was held to appear before a Judge.
No explosives were located, and police confirmed there was never any danger to the travelling public.

DRIVER CAUGHT TRAVELLING 164 KM/H ON TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY
(Nov 27th)
A 41-year-old woman had her vehicle seized and driver’s licence suspended after being caught travelling well above the posted speed limit on the Trans-Canada Highway Thursday night (Nov. 26).
A member of the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) observed the vehicle travelling at 164 km/h in a posted 100 km/h zone.
As a result, the female driver was ticketed, her vehicle was seized, and her driver’s licence was suspended.

TWO PEOPLE ARRESTED FOLLOWING STRING OF THEFTS ON THE NORTHEAST AVALON
(Nov 26th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) has charged two people who were wanted in connection with a series of recent thefts on the Northeast Avalon, including a theft valued at approximately $13,000 from a St. John’s jewellery store.
On Wednesday, November 25, around 4:00 p.m., officers responded to a tip from the public and located wanted individuals Taylor Seigmiller, 28, and James Peach, 30, at a residence in Conception Bay South.
Both individuals were arrested on outstanding warrants for failing to comply with an appearance notice related to theft charges.
During the investigation, Seigmiller was also identified as being responsible for a theft on September 10 and a $13,000 theft from a St. John’s jewellery store on October 1. Previous attempts by police to locate her had been unsuccessful.
As a result, Seigmiller was additionally charged with theft over $5,000 and theft under $5,000.
Both individuals were held to appear in court.
The RNC continues to encourage anyone who witnesses suspicious activity to report it directly to police at 709-729-8000. Crimes in progress should be reported by calling 911.

RCMP CONTINUES SEARCH FOR WANTED FEMALE
(Nov 26th)
Burin Peninsula RCMP is renewing its request for assistance locating 51-year-old Jodi Lynn Lake. Lake is the subject of an arrest warrant and continues to actively evade police.
She is approximately 5’ 11” (180 cm) tall, and 145 lbs (66 kg) with brown hair and blue eyes. Police believe Lake may be in the St. John’s metro region or in the Burin area.
Lake is wanted for failing to attend court in connection Criminal Code charges including breaking and entering, theft and failing to comply with undertaking for the purpose of Identification of Criminals Act.
If you have information regarding the current location of Jodi Lake, please dial 911, contact police at 1-800-709-RCMP (7267) or call your local police detachment as soon as possible.

24-HOUR SNOW CLEARING TO EXPAND ACROSS ENTIRE TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY
(Nov 26th)
The provincial government has announced plans to expand 24-hour snow clearing and ice control operations along the entire Trans-Canada Highway in Newfoundland, extending from St. John’s to Port aux Basques.
The proposed expansion would see more than 1,300 additional kilometres of highway receive round-the-clock winter maintenance.
The expansion will depend on the recruitment of additional highway maintenance operators.
The move would extend overnight and early-morning snow clearing and ice control coverage across the province’s main highway corridor, providing additional winter maintenance for motorists travelling during the winter months.

RNC REAFFIRMS COMMITMENT TO SUPPORT VICTIMS OF INTIMATE PARTNER VIOLENCE
(Nov 26th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is reaffirming its commitment to supporting victims and survivors of intimate partner violence, while continuing efforts to help end violence against women and girls.
The RNC says its Intimate Partner Violence Unit continues to provide support to individuals experiencing intimate partner violence and works alongside community partners to help break down barriers faced by victims of abuse.
Police say control and intimidation can create significant barriers for victims, and the RNC remains dedicated to connecting vulnerable individuals with resources and support services throughout the community.
The RNC is also encouraging anyone who suspects someone may be living in an abusive environment to reach out, noting that police are available to listen and help support victims and survivors.
Anyone experiencing violence at the hands of a partner is encouraged to contact the RNC’s Intimate Partner Violence Unit at 709-729-8093, when it is safe to do so.
The unit can also be reached at the same number for support and direction to available resources.

MISSING 13 YEAR OLD - LABRADOR
(Nov 26th)
~ 11:35 a.m; Police in Sheshatshiu are asking for the public’s help locating 13-year-old Micah Michel.
He was last seen at the local youth centre on Wednesday, November 25 around 9:30 p.m, wearing a black hooded sweatshirt, black pants, black shoes and a Toronto Blue Jays hat.
Police are concerned for his well-being and would like to speak to him as soon as possible.
If you have information about his current location, please contact Sheshatshiu RCMP as soon as possible at 709-495-8700 or call 1-800-709-RCMP (7267).
